description: Use this when the user wants printable nonogram puzzles (griddlers, hanjie, paint by numbers logic puzzles, pixel puzzles) as a PDF with an answer key: "make a nonogram", "nonogram generator", "turn this pixel art into a nonogram", "printable nonograms for my class". Put one object per puzzle in puzzles[]: shape (a built-in picture such as heart, cat, rocket), text (a word up to 8 letters), grid (the user's own rows, # filled, . empty, up to 25 x 25), or difficulty/size for a random grid; for a set of random puzzles use count with difficulty. A line solver checks that each puzzle has one solution; when a picture's clues allow several, fix decides: hints (default, print starter cells), change (flip a few cells) or refuse (error listing the unclear rows). Layout: per_page 1, 2 or 4, Letter or A4, title, name line, answer pages. Does not make colour nonograms, read photos or image files, or solve a puzzle from a photo.

answer_key.description: Add answer pages with the filled picture (default true). Example: true

count.description: How many random puzzles when they are all the same kind (1 to 12, default 1). Example: 4

difficulty.description: Difficulty of random puzzles: easy, medium (default), hard or expert. Example: hard

fix.description: For pictures and words whose clues allow more than one solution: hints (default), change or refuse. Example: refuse

grid.description: The user's own picture for a single puzzle, one string per row, # filled, . empty, up to 25 x 25. Example: [".#.#.", "#####", ".###.", "..#.."]

name_line.description: Print a Name and Date line (default true). Example: false

paper.description: letter (default, US 8.5 x 11 in) or a4. Example: a4

per_page.description: Puzzles per printed page: 1 (default), 2 or 4. Example: 2

difficulty.description: Random puzzle difficulty: easy (10 x 10), medium (15 x 15, default), hard (20 x 20) or expert (25 x 25). Example: easy

fix.description: When the clues allow more than one solution: hints (default, print a few starter cells), change (flip a few cells) or refuse (return an error listing the unclear rows). Example: hints

grid.description: The user's own pixel picture, one string per row, # for filled and . for empty (also X/1 and 0/-), up to 25 x 25. Example: ["..##..", ".####.", "######", ".#..#."]

label.description: Caption printed above this puzzle. Example: Puzzle A

seed.description: Seed for this puzzle (random puzzles and starter-cell choice). Example: 42

shape.description: A built-in picture: heart, star, house, cat, dog, fish, tree, smiley, apple, rocket, umbrella, note, anchor, duck, flower, crown, key, bell, moon, ghost. Example: heart

size.description: Size of a random puzzle, columns x rows, 5 to 25. Example: "15x15"

text.description: A short word drawn in block letters (A-Z, 0-9, up to 8 letters; 5 to 8 letters use two lines). Example: CAT

puzzles.description: One object per puzzle when they differ, e.g. [{"shape":"heart"},{"text":"MOM"},{"grid":[".##.","####",".##."]},{"difficulty":"hard"}]. Leave out and use count for a set of random puzzles. Up to 12.

seed.description: Starting seed; puzzle N uses seed + N - 1. Reuse it to reprint the same puzzles. Example: 2026

shape.description: Built-in picture for a single puzzle: heart, star, house, cat, dog, fish, tree, smiley, apple, rocket, umbrella, note, anchor, duck, flower, crown, key, bell, moon, ghost. Example: cat

size.description: Size of random puzzles, columns x rows, 5 to 25. Example: "10x10"

text.description: A short word to draw as a single puzzle (A-Z, 0-9, up to 8 letters). Example: LOVE

title.description: Title printed at the top of each page. Example: Friday Logic Puzzles

name: generate_nonograms
title: Generate printable nonograms
